summary: Same pattern and same machinery — bouncing white-tipped rainbow comets with fading trails, identical spatial-period-vs-dial mapping and identical dial thresholds — but the port's comet head travels ~1.28x too fast, its trail decays ~34% too slowly, its head clips to pure white 255 instead of the original's 234, and it winds ~1.4x more hue per trail, so the whole strip reads brighter, denser and busier than the original.
observations: Both sides compile and run clean (no compileError/runtimeError) on all runs; both expose exactly the same control surface: sliderRainbow (slider, 'Rainbow') and sliderNumber (slider, 'Number'). No control-surface mismatch.

Pattern anatomy (read from --pixels 300/600 --dump, sliderNumber=0.2-0.4): each 'rainbow' is a comet head that sweeps along the strip and bounces at the half-period boundary, leaving a trail of discrete lit points that fade geometrically. On both sides the trail points are deposited at an identical rate (8 new lit pixels per 0.1 s at 300 px, 8 per 0.2 s at 600 px — byte-equal lit COUNTS at every sampled time during trail growth) and both bounce at the same position (orig turns at px ~74/300, port at ~72/300 with sliderNumber=0.2; orig at ~300/600, port at ~300/600 with sliderNumber=0.1).

HEAD SPEED (the biggest divergence): at --pixels 600, sliderNumber=0.1, sliderRainbow=0.75 the orig head runs px 4 -> 297 in 3.2 s (~92 px/s) and reverses at t~3.3 s; the port covers the same span by t~2.55 s (~117 px/s) and has already reversed by t=2.8 s. Ratio 1.28x. Reproduced independently at --pixels 300, sliderNumber=0.2 (orig ~45 px/s turning at t~1.6 s, port ~58 px/s turning at t~1.3 s) — same 1.28x.

TRAIL LENGTH / DECAY: at saturation the orig trail holds 88 lit points (600 px, Number=0.1) vs the port's 118-122 — 1.36x. Reading the geometric ramp off a --dump at --pixels 300, Number=0.4: orig V per trail step = 0.40 0.43 0.47 0.51 0.56 0.60 0.66 0.71 0.78 0.84 0.92 (per-step fade factor ~0.921, head 234/255); port = 0.54 0.57 0.61 0.65 0.69 0.73 0.78 0.83 0.88 0.94 1.00 (fade factor ~0.940, head 255/255). Same 11-step geometric shape, wrong constants.

BRIGHTNESS / CLIPPING: untouched 6 s baseline meanBrightness avg orig 82.7 vs port 128.5 (+55%); at matched dials (Rainbow=0.75, Number=0.5, 30 s window) orig 110 vs port 145 (+32%). On a 60 px default-rig --dump the port has exactly 10 pixels railed at 255 and 10 near-white (sat<0.25, V>150) in EVERY frame sampled, while the orig never exceeds V=234 and has ZERO near-white pixels. The original's negative space reads black; the port's reads white — visible directly in the 240 s survey waterfalls.

SPACING/DUTY: because the port's head is faster while depositing at the same rate, its trail points sit ~2.9 px apart vs the original's ~2.3 px at 300 px (orig lit indices 2,4,6,9,11,13,16,18,20,22,25 vs port 2,5,8,11,14,17,20,22,25,28,31 at Number=0.2). The dark core between the two mirrored ramps of a leaf is correspondingly narrower on the port (11 px vs 23 px inside a 75 px period at Number=0.4).

HUE WINDING: with sliderRainbow in its high state, hue advances along the trail. Per trail point the orig advances ~0.128-0.138 of a turn, the port ~0.165-0.211 — 1.3x to 1.5x more, measured at three separate times. Per rainbow ramp the orig winds ~1.22 hue turns, the port ~1.74. So the port's leaves show noticeably more colour cycles. With sliderRainbow low, both sides hold a single hue along the trail (orig 0.08, port 0.07) — that part matches.

SPATIAL PERIOD vs sliderNumber MATCHES EXACTLY. Circular autocorrelation of the dumped frame at 60 px: Number 0.25 -> period 20 both sides; 0.5 -> 10 both; 0.75 -> 20 both; 1 -> 5 both. Same at 300 px: 0.2 -> 150 both, 0.3 -> 100 both, 0.4 -> 75 both, 0.5 -> 50 both, 0.8 -> 100 both, 0.9 -> 30 both. (An earlier exact-repeat metric said 15 vs 10 at 60 px; that was a measurement artefact — autocorrelation on the same dumps agrees.)

UNTOUCHED DEFAULT DIFFERS: with no control set, at 300 px the orig draws 4 rainbows (spatial period 75, autocorr 1.0) and the port draws 5 (period 60). At 60 px this is the visible '4 columns of leaves vs 5-6' difference in the untouched survey images. Neither default is reachable from the other side's dial sweep, so this is an internal-default divergence, not a dial-mapping shift.

sliderNumber=0 DIVERGES: the original goes completely black (meanBrightness 0, zero lit pixels at 60 px and at 300 px); the port still draws one full rainbow (22 lit points at 300 px, mean 31-43) and renders byte-identically to its own Number=0.1. The port's Number dial has a floor of 1 rainbow where the original's floor is 0.

sliderRainbow is a 2-state switch on BOTH sides with the SAME boundary: a 21-point sweep at 0.00..1.00 step 0.05 (Number pinned at 1, 60 px, dump at t=0.5) hashes to exactly two clusters per side, breaking between 0.50 and 0.55 on the original AND on the port. Effect magnitude also matches (mean |diff| between the 0-state and 1-state renders ~36-42 on orig, ~32-43 on port across t=0,1,5,10,19 s).

NO MODE/REGIME STRUCTURE on either side: a 240 s / 2 fps survey shows one uniform texture start to finish on both sides, no banding, no palette walk boundary, no blackout. brightnessTrend 'steady' on both in every run; zeroMotionFrames 1-2 (just the first captured frame).

NEITHER SIDE IS FRAME-RATE COUPLED. Cross-fps rescale fit on meanBrightness (corr(series_fps40[i], series_fps20[k*i]) maximized over k) returns k=0.50 for both sides, and again k=0.50 for the 20-vs-10 fps pair. (Raw autocorrelation lags are misleading here — the port posts a 35-frame peak at 10, 20 AND 40 fps, which looks frame-stepped but is a harmonic of a beat between two time-based components; the rescale fit settles it.)

Temporal rhythm at matched dials (Rainbow=0.75, Number=0.5, 60 px, 30 s at 20 fps): both sides oscillate with a fast cycle of ~11 frames — orig exactly 11 (0.55 s), port ~11.7 (0.58 s) — plus a shared slow component at 131 frames, beating into a 273-frame super-cycle on the orig and a 166-frame one on the port. The fast rhythms are within ~6% of each other; the super-cycle difference is a consequence of that, not an independent bug.
Seed-independent: seed 1234 at matched dials gives orig mean 108 / motion 24 and port 143 / 27, matching seed 1 (110/24 and 144/27). The pattern is deterministic, not RNG-driven.

Re-rendered on a 16x16 grid rig the divergence shows as slope: the port's reshaped trail draws clean steep diagonals while the orig's is denser and closer to vertical — the same root cause (trail point spacing 2.9 vs 2.3 px), not a separate finding.

dials.name: sliderRainbow
dials.origEffect: Two-state switch, boundary between 0.50 and 0.55. Low state: every point in a trail shares one hue (a single-colour comet). High state: hue advances along the trail, ~0.128-0.138 turn per trail point (~1.22 hue turns per rainbow ramp). No effect on brightness, count or geometry.
dials.portEffect: Same two-state switch with the SAME boundary between 0.50 and 0.55, and the same qualitative low/high behaviour. Differs only in the high state's hue rate: ~0.165-0.211 turn per trail point (~1.74 turns per ramp), i.e. 1.3x-1.5x too much colour winding.

dials.name: sliderNumber
dials.origEffect: Sets how many rainbows tile the strip. 0 -> completely black (zero rainbows). 0.1 -> 1, 0.2 -> 2, 0.3 -> 3, 0.4 -> 4, 0.5 -> 6 (measured as spatial period 600/N at --pixels 300 and 60). Also raises overall mean brightness monotonically (60 px: 0 / 64 / 105 / 130 / 149 at 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1).
dials.portEffect: Identical spatial-period mapping at every value from 0.1 up (verified at 60 px and 300 px). Two differences: (a) at 0 the port does NOT go dark — it still draws 1 rainbow and is byte-identical to its own 0.1 setting, so the bottom of the dial has a dead zone; (b) at every setting the port's render is 25-40% brighter than the original's (60 px: 37 / 90 / 138 / 165 / 184 at 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1).

feedback: Comet head speed is ~1.28x too fast. Measured on the default-relative geometry at --pixels 600 with sliderNumber=0.1: the original's head crosses 0 -> 300 px in ~3.25 s (~92 px/s) and the port does it in ~2.55 s (~117 px/s). Slow the head by a factor of ~0.78. Everything else about the sweep is already right — both sides bounce at the same position and deposit trail points at the same rate per second, so this is purely the traversal rate.

Trail decay is too slow: the original fades each successive trail point by a factor of ~0.921 (V sequence 0.92 0.84 0.78 0.71 0.66 0.60 0.56 0.51 0.47 0.43 0.40 from head backwards), the port by ~0.940 (1.00 0.94 0.88 0.83 0.78 0.73 0.69 0.65 0.61 0.57 0.54). Steepen the fade to ~0.92 per step; that also fixes the trail being 1.36x too long (88 lit points at saturation on the original vs 118-122 on the port at --pixels 600) and most of the 'not enough black between the leaves' impression.

The comet head is one fade step too bright: the original's brightest pixel is 234/255 (V=0.918) and never reaches 255 — a 60 px --dump of the original has ZERO pixels at or above 250 in any frame, while the port has exactly 10 railed at 255 in every frame. Start the head at ~234 rather than full 255 (equivalently, apply one decay step before the head is drawn). This is what makes the port's negative space read white where the original's reads black.

Hue advance along the trail is ~1.4x too fast when sliderRainbow is in its high state: the original winds ~1.22 hue turns across one rainbow ramp (~0.128-0.138 turn per deposited point), the port winds ~1.74 (~0.165-0.211 per point). Reduce the per-point hue step to about 0.70x its current value. The low state (single hue per trail) is already correct on both sides.

sliderNumber=0 must render completely black. The original draws zero rainbows at 0 (meanBrightness exactly 0, no lit pixels at 60 px or 300 px); the port draws one rainbow at 0 and is byte-identical to its own 0.1 setting. The count mapping from 0.1 upward is already exact (0.1->1, 0.2->2, 0.3->3, 0.4->4, 0.5->6 rainbows on both sides) — only the zero end is off, so it looks like a max/clamp or a +1 on the count that should not be there at the bottom of the range.

The untouched (no control set) default rainbow count is wrong: the original starts with 4 rainbows across the strip (spatial period 75 at --pixels 300), the port with 5 (period 60). Set the port's initial Number-backed global so it produces 4, not 5. This is the most immediately visible untouched difference — 4 columns of leaves vs 5.

Do NOT change: spatial-period-vs-dial mapping, sliderRainbow's threshold location (between 0.50 and 0.55 on both sides), the bounce/turnaround positions, the trail-point deposition rate per second, the absence of frame-rate coupling, and the overall leaf/lattice geometry — all of these already match the original exactly and were confirmed across 60/300/600 px rigs, 10/20/40 fps, seeds 1 and 1234, and a 240 s window.
